newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power steady amid cooler weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power steady amid cooler weather.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. West held steady amid cooler weather in both the Northwest and Southwest, market sources said.
Higher spot natural gas prices also helped keep prices firm, they said.

Cooler Southwest temperatures are deemed bearish for prices since they translate into decreased air conditioning demand, but the seasonal downturn in Northwest temperatures means higher heating loads.
"The weather in the Northwest is supportive of prices, but we are still watching the precipitation," said one trader.
Forecasts also call for more rain in the region over the next six to 10 days, which could result in higher output of hydroelectricity.
Next-day prices at the Palo Verde substation in Arizona for peak, firm power were little changed on Wednesday at $19.50-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).
California-Oregon border (COB) prices for Thursday were also unchanged at $19.25-19.50.
Palo Verde for November was last quoted $16.80-17.25, up slightly from $16.65-16.80 on Tuesday.
November COB was quoted $17.45-17.60, compared with $17.20-17.40 on Tuesday. MidColumbia for November was quoted $17.00-17.30, up from $16.50-16.90.
